Google just redesigned how you build Android apps — and if you haven’t updated yet, you’re leaving serious productivity on the table.
If you write Android apps for a living (or even for fun), you’ve probably noticed something: Android Studio doesn’t just add new buttons anymore — it’s quietly turning into an AI-native IDE. The last two stable releases, Quail 1 and Quail 2, are proof of that shift. One laid the groundwork. The other blew the doors open.
Let’s break down what actually changed, why it matters, and which one you should be running today.
🐦 A Quick Refresher: What’s With the Bird Names?
Google names Android Studio releases alphabetically after animals — Koala, Ladybug, Meerkat, Narwhal, Otter, Panda, and now Quail. Each letter usually gets a “1,” sometimes a “2,” “3,” or a “Feature Drop” as Google ships incremental updates through the year. Quail 1 landed in June 2026, and Quail 2 followed as the next stable milestone just weeks later.
Think of it less like “major version jumps” and more like Chrome’s rolling release model — except each one still packs meaningful, IDE-changing features.
🧠 Android Studio…
